issues.description: The problem statement and solution expect a fully implemented Meal class, but the template repository contains an empty Meal.java and a separate Order.java that provides the name/ingredients implementation. This naming/type mismatch (Meal expected vs Order present) is structural: students following the problem will look for Meal functionality in the template but find an empty file, causing compilation confusion and blocking work.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the template provide a proper Meal class implementation (matching the problem description) instead of leaving Meal.java empty and providing Order.java. Options: (a) rename Order.java to Meal.java (or copy its implementation into Meal.java) and remove the extra Order class; (b) update all example code to consistently use Meal. Ensure the template Meal.java matches the constructor and getters shown in the problem statement and solution.

issues.description: The commented example in the template Main.java uses the Order type, while the problem statement and solution expect and use a Meal type. This inconsistency in example code can confuse students about which class to implement/use.
issues.suggestedFix: Update the template Main.java example to use Meal (not Order) so it matches the problem statement and solution. Ensure all example code, comments, and templates consistently reference Meal to avoid confusion.

issues.description: The problem statement consistently refers to the concept/class as 'Meal' (e.g., class diagram and examples), and the solution implements a Meal class. However, the template repository provides an 'Order' class (and an empty Meal.java). This mismatch means students looking for the 'Meal' implementation in the template will find an empty file and a differently named class, creating confusion mapping the problem requirements to the starter code.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the template use the same identifier as the problem and solution: rename or replace the template's Order class with a Meal class (move the implementation from Order.java into Meal.java and remove the empty Meal.java), or update the problem statement to refer to 'Order' consistently. Prefer keeping 'Meal' to match the solution and problem description.
